src.t: IGN, Masaru Yamamura (FromSoftware) interview, 2023

links.extra: Directed by Masaru Yamamura, who previously served as lead game designer on Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice.

links.took: FromSoftware's deep garage mech engineering balancing weight, energy drain, and weapon recoil across customizable chassis.
links.added: Revived FromSoftware's flagship high-speed Armored Core mech series with hard-lock dodging and multi-ending Rubicon missions.

links.took: Basim's character origin and Anvil engine foundation from Ubisoft's sprawling Viking RPG.
links.added: Trimmed RPG bloat back into a focused 20-hour Baghdad stealth adventure built around pickpocketing, notoriety, and black-box hits.
links.extra: Conceived originally as a Valhalla expansion before Ubisoft Bordeaux expanded it into a standalone return to series roots.

links.took: Middle Eastern walled-city rooftop traversal, crowd blending, bureau investigations, and deliberate assassination planning.
links.added: Modernized the 2007 blueprint with Eagle vision tagging, upgradeable stealth gadgets, and multi-target Assassin's Focus strikes.

links.took: Turn-based monster collecting, elemental type charts, and creature evolution battles.
links.added: Let players transform via cassette tapes, fuse any two monsters mid-battle, and exploit chemical type-reaction status combos.

src.t: Nintendo Life, Bytten Studio interview on Cassette Beasts

links.extra: Co-founders Jay Baylis and Tom Coxon designed Cassette Beasts around doing mechanics Pokémon never tried.

links.took: A dense, interconnected open overworld unlocked progressively through new movement and traversal abilities.
links.added: Wove ability-gated island exploration and dungeon puzzles directly into a monster-collecting RPG structure.

src.t: Nintendo Life, Bytten Studio interview on Cassette Beasts

links.took: Strategic Plasma Cutter limb dismemberment, diegetic spine health bars, and USG Ishimura industrial horror.
links.added: Rebuilt the ship on Frostbite as one seamless interconnected hull with peeling flesh layers, voiced Isaac, and an Intensity Director.
links.extra: Remade by EA Motive Studio with revamped zero-gravity free flight.

links.took: Modern Switch tactical grid presentation, Divine Pulse turn rewinds, and hub base preparation.
links.added: Restored the classic weapon triangle with Break disarms and let units fuse with Emblem Rings channeling past Fire Emblem heroes.

links.took: Human: Fall Flat popularized floppy physics-driven ragdoll grabbing and comedic clumsy locomotion.
links.added: Focused wobbling ragdoll physics into chaotic plush-animal brawling arenas with dropkicks, props, and shrinking hazards.

links.took: Tactical color-coded Pikmin squad management, fruit-and-treasure hauling, and split-task route planning.
links.added: Introduced rideable rescue dog Oatchi, freezing Ice Pikmin, nighttime tower-defense expeditions, and competitive Dandori Battles.

links.took: A 1990s underground research complex thrown into chaos by an interdimensional resonance containment breach.
links.added: Cast up to six co-op players as ordinary office scientists barricading hallways with filing cabinets and crafting gadgets from lab scrap.

src.t: PC Gamer, Geoff Keene (Deep Field Games) interview, 2024

links.extra: Deep Field Games pitched the game around playing the trapped Black Mesa-style scientists rather than Gordon Freeman.

links.took: Valheim popularized cooperative PvE survival crafting structured around clearing distinct biomes to unlock new tech.
links.added: Replaced wilderness forests with interconnected corporate lab sectors, tram shortcuts, and surreal portal worlds.

links.took: Greek, Norse, Egyptian, and Atlantean RTS warfare blending villagers with myth units and cataclysmic god powers.
links.added: Rebuilt visuals on the Bang Engine with reusable cooldown god powers, manual myth-unit abilities, and a larger Wonder Age.

links.took: Open-ended vocation switching at Alltrades Abbey, custom party creation, and Erdrick's foundational JRPG quest.
links.added: Rebuilt the 1988 Famicom touchstone in HD-2D with full voice acting, Monster Wrangler class, and Monster Arena battles.

links.took: Square Enix Team Asano's HD-2D visual pipeline combining classic pixel sprites with 3D lighting and depth-of-field tilt shift.
links.added: Applied the modernized diorama aesthetic to rebuild one of Japan's earliest world-spanning JRPGs.
links.extra: Produced under Tomoya Asano's HD-2D initiative with Artdink developing.

links.took: Low-poly PlayStation-era texture grit, industrial surrealism, and psychological dread over cheap jump scares.
links.added: Confined its fractured non-linear story aboard a wrecked space freighter where a stranded crew unravels in corporate neglect.

src.t: Skybox Critics, Johanna Kasurinen (Wrong Organ) interview, 2025

links.extra: Art lead Johanna Kasurinen cited childhood memories of Silent Hill and Crash Bandicoot for its PS1 visual tone.

links.took: Exploring an eerie, walled-off Exclusion Zone filled with indifferent reality-warping anomalies inspired by Roadside Picnic.
links.added: Anchored survival around repairing, upgrading, and driving an old station wagon through roguelite Pacific Northwest storm runs.

src.t: The Guardian, Alex Dracott (Ironwood Studios) interview, 2023

links.extra: Creative director Alex Dracott cited Roadside Picnic and Tarkovsky's Stalker alongside weird-fiction ecology.

links.took: The calendar-driven Social Link structure, Tartarus tower crawling, and Dark Hour existential themes.
links.added: Remade the 2006 PS2 classic in Unreal Engine 4 with full direct party control, Theurgy burst skills, and expanded Link Episodes.

links.took: Atlus P-Studio's kinetic UI menus, Baton Pass turn handoffs, and modern dungeon quality-of-life pacing.
links.added: Retrofitted Persona 5's snappy Shift combat flow and stylish menu flair onto Persona 3's tragic story.

links.took: Team Ninja's multi-stance weapon switching, stamina-recovery Ki Pulses, and demanding parry timing.
links.added: Moved from mission-based dark fantasy into open-world Bakumatsu Japan with grappling hooks, gliders, and historical faction choices.

links.took: Historical Japanese open-world horseback exploration, samurai duels, and region-liberation camps.
links.added: Shifted to 1860s Western-contact Yokohama and Edo with faster multi-weapon parry chains and switchable mission allies.

links.took: Harsh survival ballistics, bolt-throwing anomaly navigation, artifact hunting, and emergent A-Life Zone factions.
links.added: Unified the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone into a single seamless Unreal Engine 5 open world with branching faction endings.
links.extra: Completed by Ukrainian studio GSC Game World amid the ongoing war.

links.took: Binaural 3D voice audio depicting psychosis, perspective-matching rune puzzles, and close-quarters cinematic sword duels.
links.added: Pushed Unreal Engine 5 photorealism across 10th-century Iceland with one-on-one motion-captured combat and giant encounters.

links.took: Grezzo's miniature toybox top-down Zelda engine, bright diorama art direction, and dungeon-room readability.
links.added: Made Princess Zelda the playable hero who solves puzzles and fights by conjuring Echo copies of objects and monsters.

links.took: Open-ended, player-invented physics solutions where multiple tools solve any obstacle.
links.added: Brought Tears of the Kingdom's multiplicative problem-solving philosophy back into a classic top-down Zelda adventure.

links.took: Seamlessly shifting between flat 2D plane traversal and a 3D environment to bypass puzzles.
links.added: Turned an illustrated children's picture book on a kid's desk into a portal-hopping action adventure where you rearrange story words.

src.t: Nintendo Life, The Plucky Squire hands-on & James Turner interview

links.extra: Co-directed by former Pokémon art director James Turner at All Possible Futures.

links.took: Real-time overworld squad marching where multi-unit formations clash in automated tactical battles.
links.added: Layered Vanillaware's hand-painted 2D art over programmable conditional gambit tactics and over sixty recruitable classes.

src.t: Persona Central, Takafumi Noma (Vanillaware) developer interview

links.extra: Director Takafumi Noma spent a decade realizing a modern heir to 1990s real-time tactical RPGs.

links.took: Genshin Impact popularized free-to-play open-world anime action RPGs with four-character party swapping and gacha banners.
links.added: Emphasized faster parry-and-dodge combat, parkour wall running, and equippable Echo monster abilities captured in the wild.

links.took: HoYoverse's stage-based, rapid tag-in character action combat built around dodge slows and combo switches.
links.added: Shifted to a retro-urban post-apocalyptic city with parry-assist swaps, stun Chain Attacks, and expressive cartoon animation.

links.took: Co-op looter-shooter gun variety, manufacturer quirks, and multi-tree Vault Hunter builds.
links.added: Opened planet Kairos into a seamless world with grappling hooks, double jumps, gliding, and mix-and-match licensed weapon parts.

links.took: Three Kingdoms one-versus-thousands melee battlefields driven by shifting officer morale and Musou gauges.
links.added: Refocused on a single nameless protagonist with parry-and-dodge officer duels and colossal coordinated troop charges.

links.took: Hangar 13's linear, cinema-first period crime storytelling rooted in classic Mafia atmosphere.
links.added: Moved the story to 1900s Sicily with horseback travel, knife duels, and an intimate prequel origin for the mob.

links.took: Cold War jungle camouflage, field wound surgery, stamina hunting, and Naked Snake's 1964 espionage story.
links.added: Rebuilt every jungle zone in Unreal Engine 5 with persistent mud-and-scar wear and optional over-the-shoulder modern controls.

links.took: First-person alien world scanning, visor switching, lock-on beam combat, and interconnected Morph Ball exploration.
links.added: Introduced Samus's new psychic abilities on planet Viewros alongside high-frame-rate and mouse-style Switch 2 controls.
links.extra: Returned Retro Studios to the first-person Metroid series eighteen years after Metroid Prime 3.

links.took: Joe Musashi's kunai throws, double-jump somersaults, and screen-wide Ninjutsu spells against NEO Zeed.
links.added: Expanded stages into semi-open exploration layouts with combo execution finishers and hand-drawn 2D animation.

links.took: Lizardcube's fluid hand-drawn 2D comic art pipeline and crisp Sega arcade revival sensibility.
links.added: Applied its brush-ink art craft and modern combo canceling from beat 'em ups to 2D ninja action-platforming.

links.took: Modernized Unreal Engine skate physics, revert-to-manual combo links, and faithful two-minute goal remasters.
links.added: Rebuilt the third and fourth installments' classic parks with cross-platform multiplayer and newly added skate stages.
links.extra: Developed by Iron Galaxy on the modern revival blueprint established by Vicarious Visions.

links.took: Two Point Studios' whimsical British management humor, room-template building, and guest-need balancing.
links.added: Shifted management to curating museum wings, sending staff on risky relic expeditions, and protecting exhibits from thieves.
